answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring every identity to lock a unique computational stake verified through a multi-party prism of peer challenges. Creating N identities forces the attacker to solve N independent quartz-hard puzzles whose difficulty scales with network activity; under a sudden gale of concurrent attestations the marginal cost rises from ~10^3 to >10^5 compute units per extra identity, while honest agents pay only a one-time base lock.
